messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: Elevated prefix cache miss rate for tenant=aurora in vpc-us-west-2-dedicated. 15m hit-rate down 72% -> potential cache pollution or prefetch storm. Paging on-call.

Samira Patel: got the page. I'm oncall. starting triage — can someone pull the per-prefix hit-rate and the prefetch queue sizes?

Luis Ortega: pulling metrics now. prefix "user:" shows hit-rate drop from 91 -> 18 over last 12m. prefetch queue length jumped to ~48k on pool-a-1. sending graphs to #eng-sre.

Ben Chu: confirming. hitting fallback path: many requests are being routed to fallback_model-small which is CPU-bound. latency p50 -> 220ms, p95 -> 1.8s for aurora. top observed symptom is persistent KV miss on prefix user:.

Priya Mehta: customer impact: Aurora production showing ~35% error budget burn for requests that exceed latency SLO. They reported user-visible slowdowns ~10:45 PDT, started escalating to account team.

Samira Patel: thanks. initial hypothesis: tenant-specific cache prefetch policy (aggressive prefetch on long tail) combined with a bursty workload created prefix noise and evicted hot prefixes. Could be tenant-level prefetch enabled + large cold prefixes.

Ben Chu: I see repeated prefix churn in logs, lots of unique prefixes from Aurora in short window. Likely cache pollution from a batch job.

Luis Ortega: running a targeted prefix list query: top noisy prefixes: user:session:, user:history:, tmp:batch:job:. suspect tmp:batch:job.

Samira Patel: mitigation plan (short): 1) disable prefetch for tenant aurora. 2) temporarily pin dedicated pool routing to bypass prefetch layer for aurora. 3) flush small set of noisy prefixes. 4) communicate to customer and CRO.

Priya Mehta: will draft customer message. immediate ask: give us a 15m window for mitigation and we'll update.

Luis Ortega: disabling prefetch for tenant aurora now:

```
redwood-admin prefetch set --tenant aurora --enabled false --scope tenant
```

Luis Ortega: prefetch disabled acknowledged by control plane. verifying queue drain...

ops-bot: control-plane: prefetch disable command accepted for tenant=aurora (txn=0x7c4f). queue drain started.

Ben Chu: draining prefetch queues shows inbound rate of 1.2k/s but backlog is shrinking.

Samira Patel: next: prepare targeted prefix flush for the noisy prefixes. we DO NOT want to flush entire tenant cache. doing targeted flush for tmp:batch:job and tmp:batch:job/* first. Ben/luis can you run a dry-run to list keys that would be evicted?

Ben Chu: dry-run lists ~14.9k keys under tmp:batch:job.* — many are ephemeral. ok to evict.

Luis Ortega: running targeted flush:

```
redwood-admin kv flush-prefix --tenant aurora --prefix "tmp:batch:job" --dry-run=false --confirm
```

ops-bot: kv-flush job started (job_id=kv-33721). staging nodes will handle evictions gradually to avoid thundering.

Samira Patel: monitor request latencies and hit-rate. roll back if anything weird. alert me on >5% error increase.

Ben Chu: after ~90s we see prefix hit-rate for user: up from 18 -> 64. overall tenant hit-rate improved 72% -> 86%. p95 latency falling from 1.8s -> 420ms.

Priya Mehta: sending note to account team and Aurora primary contact: "We've disabled prefetch for your tenant and evicted noisy batch prefixes; performance improvements seen. We'll monitor and follow up with root cause."

Samira Patel: good. next: longer-term mitigation ideas to propose in notes: 1) prefetch rate limits per tenant, 2) TTL caps for prefetch-generated keys, 3) telemetry alerting on prefix-churn for each tenant, 4) autoscaling knobs for dedicated pools in presence of prefetch storms.

Luis Ortega: logging shows a scheduled Aurora job that creates a large set of ephemeral prefixes around 10:30 PDT — I'll raise an RFC to add a tenant prefetch-safety throttle.

Ben Chu: also putting in a hotfix to change eviction priority: mark prefixes created by prefetch with lower promotion priority to avoid evicting established hot prefixes. small change to KV TTL metadata.

Samira Patel: handoff plan: I'm staying until hit-rate >85% and p95 <500ms for 30m. After that I'll hand to next oncall (Priya) at 02:00 UTC. Please include checklist: monitored dashboards, kv-eviction job id, control-plane txn id, change log.

Priya Mehta: ACK. I'll pick up at handoff and coordinate cross-functional write-up and postmortem.

ops-bot: incident-log: mitigation actions recorded (prefetch_disable_txn=0x7c4f, kv_flush_job=kv-33721, started_by=Luis Ortega).

Samira Patel: one more thing — reach out to Aurora SRE to ask if they kicked off a batch job. Ben please get exact time window and program name. We'll coordinate a joint RCA.

Ben Chu: on it. I have logs indicating a cron job aurora-batch-regen ran at 10:29:06 PDT creating temp prefixes. I'll share a snippet in #customer-bridge.

Samira Patel: ok team, thanks for fast action. keeping thread open for updates.

Priya Mehta: follow-up action items for postmortem: - timeline with metrics - customer-facing explanation - code change proposal for prefetch throttling - dedicated pool autoscale test - post-deploy verification steps.

Ben Chu: closing loop: p95 now 330ms, overall hit-rate 89%. will watch for 15m stable window.

Samira Patel: handing to Priya at 02:00 UTC — Priya you have the keys.

Priya Mehta: taking handoff. will run 15m monitoring runbook and schedule postmortem 1:1 with eng-sre + product.

incident-bot: Incident resolved (status=mitigated) — latency and hit-rate recovered. Incident duration ~1h 10m.

Samira Patel: final note: avoid tenant-wide cache flush unless necessary. targeted prefix evictions + prefetch disable worked here.

Priya Mehta: filing postmortem ticket: RDW-INC-20412. Assigning to Ben for timeline + to Luis for control-plane recommendations.

Ben Chu: thanks — I'll attach log excerpts and the kv-eviction job record.

Samira Patel: great work everyone. :thumbsup:
